statements.text: You have previously studied relation between two variables x, y
In each ordered pair (a, b), a is called the first projection and b is called the second projection.
Each ordered pair is represented by one and only one point in the coordinate plane.
If a ≠ b then (a, b) ≠ (b, a). The page asks 'Why?' with no printed answer. Formula: $a\neq b \Rightarrow (a, b)\neq(b, a)$
The ordered pair (a, b) is not equal to the set {a, b}. Formula: $(a, b)\neq\{a, b\}$
If (a, b) = (x, y) then a = x and b = y. Formula: $(a, b)=(x, y)\Rightarrow a=x, \ b=y$

context.text: Imagine two cinema tickets show the seat as (row, seat number). Sara's ticket says $(x-2, \,3)$ and her brother's ticket says $(5, \,y+1)$, and the cashier says both tickets are for exactly the same seat. Work out the values of $x$ and $y$.

statements.text: If X and Y are two finite non-empty sets then X×Y = {(a, b) : a ∈ X, b ∈ Y}. Formula: $X\times Y=\{(a, b):a\in X, \ b\in Y\}$
X×Y ≠ Y×X where X ≠ Y. Formula: $X\times Y\neq Y\times X$
The number of elements of X×Y equals that of Y×X, which equals n(X) times n(Y). Formula: $n(X\times Y)=n(Y\times X)=n(X)\times n(Y)$
n denotes the number of set elements.
If (k, m) ∈ X×Y then k ∈ X and m ∈ Y. Formula: $(k, m)\in X\times Y\Rightarrow k\in X, \ m\in Y$
If X is a non-empty set then X×X = {(a, b) : a, b ∈ X}. Formula: $X\times X=\{(a, b):a, b\in X\}$
X×X is written X² and read "X two". Formula: $X\times X=X^2$
If n(X) = 3, then n(X × X) = 3 × 3 = 9. Formula: $n(X)=3\Rightarrow n(X\times X)=3\times3=9$

context.text: Suppose a bus company numbers its two starting stations $X=\{1, 2\}$ and its three towns $Y=\{3, 4, 5\}$, and every station has a direct bus to every town. The manager wants a poster of all the routes. Write the routes as ordered pairs, then show how you would draw them with arrows from stations to towns, and as points on a grid.

statements.text: Step 1: Draw two perpendicular straight lines, one of them the line x'x horizontally and the other y'y vertically, intersecting at point O.
Step 2: Represent the natural numbers N on each of the horizontal and vertical straight lines, starting with the origin point O which represents the number zero.

Step 3: Draw vertical and horizontal straight lines from the points representing the natural numbers; the points of intersection of these lines are represented by the perpendicular graphical net of the cartesian product N × N.
Notice that: each point of this net represents one of the ordered pairs in the cartesian product of N × N.
Each point of the net represents one of the pairs in the cartesian product Z × Z.
This net is known as the coordinate plane of Z × Z.
The horizontal straight line xx' is called the x-axis.
The vertical straight line yy' is called the y-axis.
